summary: Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2007) under Jing Yin, and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.
Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who taught Constance E. Kassor. He has held posts at Sakya College and as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, and Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery and taught Dagpo Rinpoche and Thubten Jigme Norbu.

Ngawang Wangyal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Agvan Dorjiev and earned a geshe degree at Drepung Monastery. He taught at Columbia University (~1962–1974) and the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983).

Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khenpo Shenga.

Ngulchu Dharmabhadra was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, later teaching numerous disciples.
Nguyen Thi Tuyet specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at Punjabi University under Inder Mohan Singh (attested 2012) and also studied under Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at Punjabi University under Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor K. T. S. Sarao.
Nhu Lien works in Buddhist studies, having studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under Ādiccavaṃsa.

Nianzu Huang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia and Hsu Yun. He served as professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications and head of Central People's Broadcasting Station.

Nichidatsu Fujii worked in Buddhist and religious studies, founding Nipponzan-Myōhōji. He studied at institutions including Rissho University, Jodo Shu Daigakuin, Kogi Shingonshu Rengo Kyoto Gakurin, Hōryūji Kingakuin, Shingonshu Rengo Daigaku, and Kennin-ji.

Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974), the Post Graduate Institute of Buddhist Studies at Vidyalankara Campus, and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Nicholas Dirks is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). He held faculty posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Rodney Needham. He was a lecturer at Durham University (1972–1976) and later Reader in the Social Anthropology of South Asia at Oxford (1976, 1997).

Nicholas Poppe was a linguist and Central Asian scholar who studied under Boris Vladimirtsov at the University of Saint Petersburg. He held professorships there (1923–1941) and later served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich was an artist and scholar in history and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Imperial Academy of Arts and the University of Saint Petersburg, later serving as director of the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts (~1906–1917).
